authority.approval: user, 2026-09-26: implement the campaign, run one capped integration pilot and the six campaign runs if every launch and integrity gate passes; no pause between them

question: After +1,536,000 policy-controlled transitions from the same Phase K reward-v2 checkpoint, does training with anchored backward starts cut from the one registered sweep (arm E) make normal tick-0 play break all seven right targets by consumed tick 2699 more often than the same training with tick-0 starts only (arm K), without losing static targets?

arms.E: m7m_e_s{0,1,2}: anchored backward starts from the registered anchor, p0 = 1/2
arms.K: m7m_k_s{0,1,2}: matched control, the same machinery, tick-0 starts only

sequencing: pilot E then K; then strictly sequential E0, K0, E1, K1, E2, K2, the launch gate before each

contracts.diagnostic_flag: SSB64_RL_TARGET_DIAG=1, read-only and gameplay-neutral, in both arms and in every evaluation; never part of the policy observation

registered_settings.warm_start: both arms of pair j load runs/m7g_k/m7g_s{j}_v1/final: policy parameters and Adam optimizer state (step 60,000) from model.zip, VecNormalize statistics continuing (training=True, observations only), num_timesteps continuing from 3,072,000 (reset_num_timesteps=False), constant learning rate 3e-4 and clip range 0.2, set_random_seed(base_seed) at load with the same base seed (100 + j) in E_j and K_j; the one accepted compatibility difference is the diagnostic flag (recorded in the lineage); a checkpoint trained with any curriculum is refused

budget.prefix_ticks: never counted as transitions; reported separately

schedule.E: anchored starts drawn after automatic resets with probability 1/2 (tick0_probability 0.5) until the schedule completes; then tick-0 starts only
schedule.K: tick0_probability 1.0: normal tick-0 starts only (the same worker, vector wrapper and logs)
schedule.cut_semantics: cut tau (1..1020): after the ordinary non-consuming tick-0 reset, anchor rows 0..tau-1 are submitted one per native tick (consumed ticks 0..tau-1); the policy's first action is for input tick tau; the horizon counts from the reset, so at most 3600 - tau policy steps; prefix breaks earn nothing (reward reference rebased on the post-prefix observation)
schedule.success: all seven right targets {0,2,3,4,5,7,9} broken, the last at consumed tick <= 2699 (for a cut, the standing right targets broken by the policy; a later fall does not undo it)
schedule.in_flight_outcomes: an anchored outcome is counted only toward the block of the window in which its episode started, and only while that window is current; episodes that started under an earlier window and finish after the pointer moved are logged as stale and never counted; lifecycle failures and aborted episodes are logged as excluded; outcomes are ingested in parent order (vector step, then environment index) before that step's draws

launch_gate.readings: a failed reading is re-measured after 60 s, at most 5 readings; the run launches only on a passing reading
launch_gate.when: before every training launch (pilot and campaign runs)

registered_settings.monitor: m7d Monitor: hard alerts stop the run (an episode row violating its prefix-aware btt_reward_v2 closed form, more than 10 game processes or listeners in two samples, a changed user config, low disk)
stop_conditions: a training or evaluation verification failure (an evaluation label may be re-run once)
registered_settings.after_a_stop: the campaign stops and reports; a stopped run directory is moved to _partial by the guard and preserved; nothing is resumed, relaunched or extended
registered_settings.training_inputs: the run's own episodes and the registered anchor's start states only; never supervised targets, other runs' weights, the crossing fixtures, TAS, feasibility or pilot outputs
registered_settings.never: native RNG state is never inspected, logged, validated, controlled, compared or hashed; no training videos

start_state_table.note: durable evidence: kept in docs, never discarded (it can be regenerated by F1, which is not a reason to drop it)

feasibility_result.classification: feasibility evidence only (never a training input or a result)

pilot.warm_start: the seed-0 Phase K final, as the campaign pair 0
checks: actual PPO updates: n_updates +80, Adam step +800 on every parameter, policy digest changed
continuation: num_timesteps 3,112,960; 8 rollout records; obs_rms count = warm + 5 + 40,960
policy-only accounting: finished-episode policy steps <= 40,960 and >= 40,960 - 5 x 3,600; prefix ticks only in the selection log; row prefix_length = outcome tau; rows = prefix + policy
E: at least one anchored start delivered equal to the table in W0, its outcome ingested; K: no anchored draw, no prefix tick
schedule state = blocks recomputed from the logged outcomes (in-flight rule)
training verification (m7d, warm-start segment), lineage = the pinned Phase K final, leak-free
the evaluation smoke: tick-0 starts, metrics clean, rows verified
pilot.never: pilot performance is never used to tune the curriculum, reward or budget; pilot outputs are never campaign inputs; each campaign run starts again from its pinned Phase K checkpoint

evaluation_protocol.clear_verification: every native clear in evaluation (m7g_k_run.verify_clears_in) and in training (exact artifact replay from tick 0)
evaluation_protocol.warm_start_reference: the Phase K final evaluations runs/m7g_k/_eval/m7g_s{j}_v1/final (read only; reported as the common starting point)
